svg.text: The attackers assemble the worm from a
ransomware component and the SMBv1 exploit
The first host is infected before the worm
spreads by itself. Sources disagree on the entry
(T1566.001*). MITRE does not state an initial
On start-up the worm tries an HTTP connection
to a hard-coded domain. If the connection
succeeds, the worm exits, so spreading and
encryption do not run on that host. The check
MITRE does not list this mapping.
service mssecsvc2.0 with the display name
The worm finds its local network segment
(T1016) and scans for systems to infect
(T1018). One thread scans the local subnet
addresses. The target is SMB on TCP/445
The worm exploits the SMBv1 vulnerability
run code and spread (T1210). In industrial
networks MITRE maps this to ICS T0866.
The worm uses the DoublePulsar backdoor to
install and run its payload on the host.
DoublePulsar is either already present or has
just been installed by the EternalBlue exploit in
step 6. MITRE does not list a technique for this
step, so only the tactic Execution (TA0002) is
The worm copies itself to the compromised
host and starts there (T1570, ICS T0867). The
new host repeats the flow from step 3.
The worm enumerates local, removable and
mapped network drives and searches for user
files by extension (T1083). It also scans for
newly attached drives and encrypts files on
The worm kills database and mail server
sqlserver.exe and Exchange, so their data files
are unlocked and can be encrypted (T1489).
The worm hides its files with ‘attrib +h’
The worm deletes shadow copies and
bcdedit and wbadmin (T1490). The use of
The helper tool taskse.exe enumerates active
Remote Desktop sessions and starts the
ransom window in each, so remote users also
see the note (T1563.002, listed by MITRE).
The worm installs Tor as taskhsvc.exe and
through a local SOCKS5 proxy (T1090.003). A
custom cryptographic protocol over the circuit is
used for key exchange and payment checks
Files are encrypted with a per-file AES-128 key
note demands $300 in Bitcoin, rising to $600 if
If a route from the infected IT network to the OT
network exists, the worm spreads to Windows
hosts in industrial networks via SMB (ICS
T0866, T0867). The step is conditional because
the spread depends on network segmentation.

infection. Loss of view (ICS T0829*) is an
